title: Electing an Optional Supplemental Benefit Rider Alongside a Medical Plan
content:
The Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders are sold only with a Ridgecrest medical plan. A rider is bought alongside a medical plan and never on its own, and only on the plan tiers the rider is sold with.

## 1. The medical plan must stand in force

The medical plan enrollment the rider names stands at active or in its premium grace period on the day the rider is accepted. This is judged before the rider is accepted, on the plan's own enrollment records — the enrollment's own reference, the member it belongs to and its standing. The enrollment looked at is the one the rider names as the plan it hangs on, and no other.

## 2. The election window

The plan receives the rider request no later than the last day of the rider enrollment window counted from the coverage effective date of that medical plan enrollment. Calendar days are counted from the day after the medical plan's coverage effective date, every day of the week counts, a request received on the final day of the window is in time, and full 24-hour periods are never used in place of calendar days. This too is judged before the request is taken, on the plan's records of the medical plan enrollment's coverage effective date and of the day the rider request was received, correlated through the enrollment the rider names.

### Boundary cases (hypothetical)

Take a rider whose enrollment window is 31 calendar days and a medical plan enrollment whose coverage began on a given day.

- A request received on the 31st day counted from the day after that coverage effective date is **in time**: the final day of the window is itself inside it.
- A request received on the 32nd day counted the same way is **out of time**: it is later than the last day of the window.

## 3. Outside the window

Outside that window a rider may be added only during the annual election period, for cover beginning the following 1 January, and the member is told that date plainly rather than being left to expect cover sooner.

## 4. The start date and the premium

The rider takes effect on the date its effective date rule produces from the day the request was received, and the premium runs from that day whether or not the waiting period has ended.

## 5. Who may ask

Only the member may ask for a rider, because it is an extra premium out of their own pocket, and the plan never adds one because a dentist or a relative asked.

## 6. Withdrawing a request

A request withdrawn before the rider takes effect leaves no rider at all and no premium is charged; a request withdrawn afterwards is a cancellation and follows the cancellation rules instead.

## 7. A member on a tier the rider is not sold with

A member on a plan tier the rider is not sold with is told which tiers carry it and when they could move, rather than having the request simply refused.
